cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 29133 male smokers aged 50-69 years from southwestern Finland were randomly assigned to receive alpha-tocopherol (50 mg), beta-carotene (20 mg), both agents, or placebo daily for 5-8 years (median, 6.1 years).
reason: The trial reports overall incident prostate cancer and prostate cancer mortality. It distinguishes clinical from latent cancer but does not define or analyze high-grade, advanced, metastatic, lethal-incidence, or another qualifying aggressive incident endpoint. Mortality among diagnosed cases is not aggressive incidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: A 32% decrease (95% confidence interval [CI] = -47% to -12%) in the incidence of prostate cancer was observed among the subjects receiving alpha-tocopherol (n = 14564) compared with those not receiving it (n = 14569).
estimate_classifications.reason: The alpha-tocopherol estimate is explicitly for overall prostate cancer incidence, not aggressive disease.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Among subjects receiving beta-carotene (n = 14560), prostate cancer incidence was 23% higher (95% CI = -4%-59%) and mortality was 15% higher (95% CI = -30%-89%) compared with those not receiving it (n = 14573).
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied beta-carotene estimate corresponds to the overall prostate cancer incidence result, not the separate mortality result and not an aggressive endpoint.
